references.text: Aaron and his sons were anointed for priestly service, establishing the concept of 'the anointed priest' (הַכֹּהֵן הַמָּשִׁיחַ)
Describes the high priest as the one who has the anointing oil on his head and his special holy status
The same offering (a young bull without defect) is required for the sin of the whole congregation, showing the seriousness of the high priest's sin
The requirement for a flawless animal (תָּמִים) as an offering to the Lord
Aaron is commanded to take a young bull as a sin offering, linking the high priest's sin offering to the consecration ritual
A young bull is used as a burnt offering when the whole congregation sins unintentionally
The ruler shall offer a bull as a sin offering for himself and the people, reflecting the priest's responsibility for the people's guilt
The high priest is appointed to present gifts and offerings for sins, and must also offer sacrifices for his own sins
The Levitical high priests had to first offer sacrifices for their own sins, then for the sins of the people
The high priest entered the Most Holy Place with blood that he offered for himself and for the sins of the people
Direct continuation of the ritual for the priest's sin offering; describes the execution of the introductory verse.
